questions.cardText:
[Anthropology] What is “cultural relativism” in anthropology?
A. Interpreting a culture by its own standards
B. The doctrine that to understand a culture, we must compare how it is different from another culture
C. The study of a culture’s difference from its past
Answer: A. This principle is foundational in anthropology but also raises ethical questions about human rights and universal standards.
questions.de: Welches Grundprinzip der Anthropologie besagt, dass eine Kultur nach ihren eigenen Maßstäben verstanden und gedeutet werden soll?
questions.en: What foundational principle of anthropology holds that a culture should be understood and interpreted by its own standards?

timeline.labelEn: Alain Locke makes the first recorded use of the term "cultural relativism"
timeline.labelDe: Alain Locke verwendet erstmals belegt den Begriff „Kulturrelativismus“

questions.notes: The idea goes back to Franz Boas (1887), who never used the phrase.

questions.cardText:
[Psychology] Which form of placebo is generally perceived as the most effective by patients?
A. Injection B. Tablet C. Capsule
Answer: A. Injections are often perceived as more powerful than capsules or tablets, even when they contain no active ingredients.
questions.de: Welche Darreichungsform eines Placebos wirkt meist stärker als Tabletten und Kapseln?
questions.en: Which form of placebo tends to have a stronger effect than both tablets and capsules?

timeline.labelEn: "Placebo" is defined as "any medicine adapted more to please than to benefit the patient"
timeline.labelDe: „Placebo“ wird definiert als „jede Medizin, die eher dem Gefallen als dem Nutzen des Patienten dient“

questions.notes: Wikipedia: capsules appear more influential than pills, and injections even stronger than capsules (Rosenberg & Kosslyn 2010).
